e569-e2e-harness.note: LANDED #579 @403e84fc. ISSUE #569. RAI RULED DIRECTLY (2026-08-28): upgrade Playwright AND Electron to the latest MUTUALLY-COMPATIBLE versions — NOT a minimal pin-back, NOT a workaround, and NOT amending C14's packet around it. Fix the harness properly. Current break: 'Electron: bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0', Electron 43.2.0 vs @playwright/test 1.62.0, failing at electron.launch BEFORE any app code runs — so it blocks EVERY Electron spec identically, including the four pre-existing ones. Pre-existing and repo-wide (controlled: an untouched spec on main fails identically), NOT caused by c20. LATEST COMPATIBLE, NOT LATEST INDEPENDENTLY — picking each side's newest in isolation is exactly how 43.2.0 met 1.62.0. If they cannot both be latest, take the newest compatible PAIR and report the constraint; never silently pick one side. Dependency standard + npmrc min-release-age=7 planned around, NOT overridden. ACCEPTANCE BAR: the four pre-existing desktop E2E specs actually RUN AND PASS (not merely that electron.launch stops erroring), plus rennet-desktop:package-smoke, plus full pnpm check with a GATE_EXIT line. c20's corner-slot spec runs as an informational fifth — its verdict is c20's business. Electron majors move Chromium, so app-level breakage (renderer APIs, daemon supervisor, apps/desktop/src/main) is IN SCOPE to fix: an upgrade that green-lights E2E while breaking the app is worse than the status quo. *** SEQUENCING PRIORITY: this is worth MORE THAN ITS OWN SCOPE. A working harness is the ONLY thing that would smoke-test the release before it auto-updates onto Rai's machine — right now NOTHING does. So it lands ahead of c21 session-mint if a choice is forced: a broken release reaching him is worse than a late one. Footprint (package.json + lockfile + apps/desktop) collides with c20, so it folds c20's main and lands AFTER c20 — implementation runs in parallel, landing serializes. Must land BEFORE the release and obviously before C14. *** Converted in-flight from a timeboxed spike; timebox lifted. ONE agent on these files. | *** FIXED @de61a1ce (GATE_EXIT=0, package-smoke PASS) — AND THE DIAGNOSIS OVERTURNED OUR WHOLE THEORY. IT WAS NEVER A VERSION MISMATCH. ROOT CAUSE: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 is exported into every shell whose parent is itself an Electron app — INCLUDING THE AGENT TERMINAL THIS BUILD RUNS IN. Both apps/desktop/e2e/harness.ts and scripts/smoke-packaged-app.mjs spread process.env into the launch, so the Electron binary ran as BARE NODE and Playwright's --remote-debugging-port hit NODE'S option parser. Bisected on the SAME electron 43 / playwright 1.62 pair: var set -> 'bad option'; env -u -> 'DevTools listening'. Fix is `delete environment.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` in two files. Rennet's own daemon spawn sets the var explicitly, so dropping the INHERITED value costs nothing. LESSON FOR THE RECORD: the version-incompatibility theory (mine and the coordinator's) was WRONG, and it would have STAYED wrong if the agent had bumped versions and declared victory when the symptom moved. A symptom moving is not a cause found. It honoured Rai's ruling anyway: playwright 1.62.1 + electron 43.4.1, the newest ELIGIBLE pair (electron 44.0.0 is 3 days old, excluded under min-release-age=7), dependency-standard table updated. *** SETUP NOTE: it ran `playwright install chromium` locally (machine-level, was absent) — capture in CI/setup docs or the next machine hits it. LANDS AFTER c20 (footprint collision on apps/desktop).

invalidation-576.note: LANDED #583 @79eba06d (closes #576). ISSUE #576. Staleness expression COPIED from mobile (projection.ts:93) minus the reachability half with the reason stated (a desktop window IS its daemon connection), so the two platforms cannot drift on the definition of stale. STALED_BY_FRESHNESS is module-level so mutate keeps stable identity and the focus effect cannot self-retrigger (the class c16's fixer hit with inline options). Fixed the #572 camouflage IN THE FILE IT TOUCHED — the C6/C8/C5 comment block that enumerated the rebuild's parts while silently omitting freshness now names it; fixing camouflage where you find it beats deferring to the sweep. Proof is DRIVEN not asserted: mounts ReviewWorkspace over a MemoryBridge whose checkFreshness returns status:'invalid', asserts the rendered text, clicks Regenerate BY ACCESSIBLE NAME, asserts the command fired with the right reviewId/repoPath, and asserts the NEGATIVE half (a current review renders nothing). Rule Zero clean: no modal, no confirm, nothing blocked. Scope held exactly — affected-only regeneration, potentially-invalid class, OID provenance all skipped. SEQUENCING: lands BEFORE F1 (smaller, already green, pure insertion); F1 rebases onto it. F1 warned to read any conflict in that file for INTENT, never by side. | REVIEW: BLOCK, three findings, ALL TAKEN. Restoration itself VERIFIED END TO END (traced mount ask -> cache invalidate -> prefix match -> refetch -> refreshed status -> render; server grants allowedRoots and starts the watcher BEFORE the mount asks, so the path is reachable not dead). Placement improvement endorsed with a check I had not thought to ask for: ExitFab's root is pointer-events-none absolute inset-0, so Regenerate is not swallowed in a REAL browser — HAPPY-DOM WOULD NEVER HAVE CAUGHT THAT. *** FINDING A, THE SERIOUS ONE AND A CATEGORY WORTH REMEMBERING: THE FIX FOR A LIE INTRODUCED TWO NEW LIES ON THE PR PATH. The freshness ask runs for EVERY review, but dispatch/review.ts:50-55 states the contract — a PR review is a SNAPSHOT, not wired to the working-tree watcher, 'the renderer gates that off by patchset source' — and NOTHING in app-ui gates on patchset.source. repositoryDirty is a single GLOBAL and review.load starts the watcher for a PR clone too. So: edit repo A with review A open -> dirty -> navigate to PR review B -> mount asks -> captures B's WORKING TREE -> cannot match B's github-local/github-rest patchset id -> ReviewInvalidated is COMMITTED TO THE STORE and the banner falsely claims the repository changed. Then Regenerate calls capture and REPLACES THE PR DIFF WITH A LOCAL WORKING-TREE CAPTURE. A UI lie + a persisted state write + DESTROYING THE ARTIFACT UNDER REVIEW. Fix: discriminator on patchset source, early-return when not local, stale = fromWorkingTree && status === 'invalid', plus the specified test. LESSON: an honesty fix applied UNIFORMLY across surfaces with different contracts manufactures dishonesty on the surfaces it did not consider. *** FINDING B, ROOT-CAUSE FIX TAKEN: chokidar is REBUILT ON EVERY WINDOW FOCUS (repo-watcher.ts:40-51 start() unconditionally closes and re-watches; every focus invalidates review.load unconditionally, refetches, calls startWatching again). Every alt-tab tears down and re-walks the repo watcher — the OPPOSITE of the 'a focus is cheap' claim the change itself wrote. With ignoreInitial:true plus the dirty-flag reset, EDITS LANDING IN THE REBUILD WINDOW ARE SILENTLY DROPPED: a stale review that never says so — THE EXACT FAILURE THIS CHANGE EXISTS TO PREVENT, REINTRODUCED BY ITS OWN MECHANISM. Fixed in the watcher (no-op when already watching the same root), which fixes every review.load caller rather than this one site. FINDING C, #572 CREATED LIVE AGAIN: STALED_BY_FRESHNESS invalidates 'review.load' while routes/slug.ts declares itself the single swap point that moves off review.load at B9 — after that swap the invalidation stops hitting the read that feeds the prop and THE BANNER SILENTLY STOPS APPEARING, with no test catching it because freshness.dom.test.tsx passes the review prop directly (proving 'the ask fires' and 'an invalid prop renders', never 'the answer refreshes the prop'). HONESTY CORRECTION FOR THE LANDING NOTE: the mobile expression is DUPLICATED, NOT SHARED, so 'cannot drift' is aspirational — the comment citing the source is the practical mitigation. Right not to over-engineer a shared helper for two call sites, but the note must not claim drift-proofing it does not have. | FIX PASS: all three taken @41a9263f (GATE_EXIT=0, each with its own control red-then-green). A CONFIRMED WORSE THAN THE REVIEW SUMMARY, BY TRACING RATHER THAN ACCEPTING: core/index.ts:990 captures the working tree UNCONDITIONALLY and compares to activePatchsetId; a github-* id can NEVER match; and regenerate is literally this.capture(...). So the false banner and the artifact replacement were CERTAIN, NOT PROBABLE. Its control replaced the gate with 'const fromWorkingTree = true' and watched BOTH PR-snapshot cases go red with the ask firing twice (mount + focus) exactly as predicted while the other four stayed green; and the test is parameterised over BOTH github-local and github-rest with status:'invalid' SEEDED DELIBERATELY — the ADVERSARIAL case, so even a PR review already carrying that status can never be narrated as 'the repository changed'. Testing the adversarial case rather than the convenient one. B FIXED AT THE ROOT in the watcher so all three startWatching callers benefit, with a test asserting a DIFFERENT root still rebuilds so the no-op cannot OVER-fire — guarding against the fix's own failure mode is the part people skip. C got both halves and the round-trip test proved cheap after all (a 4-line harness over useSlugResolution), so the B9 swap will go RED rather than silently stop showing the banner — the #572 class closed BY CONSTRUCTION at the one place we could see it coming. Honesty correction accepted verbatim: the comment now says the mobile expression is 'a COPY ... not a shared helper, so the pointer home is the only thing keeping the two honest.' Confirm pass dispatched; lands on CONFIRMED, then F1+c21 rebase onto it. | CONFIRMED then landed. Seat verified rather than assumed: A's gate is the FIRST statement in the effect, ahead of both ask() and addEventListener, so no PR review reaches checkFreshness at all — and because `stale` ANDs the same predicate, review.regenerate is unreachable for a snapshot too, so BOTH the false narration AND the artifact replacement are cut, not just the visible half; fromWorkingTree is in the dep array so a prop change re-evaluates instead of stranding a listener. ON B IT ANSWERED THE QUESTION NOBODY HAD ASKED — is discarding the new callback and locus on a same-root no-op actually SAFE? — and traced RepoWatcher.start to exactly ONE caller passing one closure and locusForRepo(root), a PURE FUNCTION OF ROOT, making the discard PROVABLY safe rather than asserted safe in a comment: the difference between a guard that works and one that happens to work. C's round-trip traced end to end (rename the key -> no prefix match -> entry never stales -> no refetch -> prop keeps 'current' -> waitFor times out, with loads > 1 as a second independent tripwire). 'A focus is cheap' in the route header is now TRUE rather than aspirational — the comment and the code finally agree, which is the whole point of #572. Verified on main: checkFreshness x4, and repo-watcher.ts carries `if (this.watcher && this.root === repositoryRoot) return;`.
